text:
Helene takes 31st victim in CSRA, a 65-year-old in Aiken County
AUGUSTA, Ga. (WRDW/WAGT) - Hurricane Helene continues to be a killer, with the latest victim being a 65-year-old man who suffered a cardiac-related death.
Richard Seigler, 65, died Saturday on C&H Lane in Aiken County north of New Ellenton, according to Aiken County Coroner Darryl Ables.
His death brings the local toll to 31.
Like many of the most recent victims of the storm, he was an older patient who died of a health condition brought on or exacerbated by the storm.
The initial deaths were from trees falling on homes and vehicles.
Some of those victims were families, like a 27-year-old mother who died with her two babies in McDuffie County and a pair of grandparents who died while hugging each other when a tree fell on their Beech Island home.
Others were first responders like a pair of Saluda County firefighters, Chad Satcher and Landon Cale Bodie, who died when a tree fell on their firetruck in the initial response to the storm.
The next wave of deaths involved vehicle accidents, like a car that hit a tree in a roadway and an incident involving a tractor.
Now we’re seeing medical-related deaths like Seigler’s.
Here’s a look at the fatalities so far across the CSRA:
Aiken County
On Oct. 7, Randy Harris, 66, died of respiratory issues at Aiken County Regional Medical Center.
On Oct. 4, Aiken County Coroner Darryl Ables announced three deaths related to Hurricane Helene. They include:
- Paul Linn, 86, of Broughton Drive, who died of respiratory issues.
- Wayne Dawes, 81, of Fairway Drive, who died of cardiac problems
- Douglas Buck, 80, of Pine Log Road, who also died of cardiac problems
On Oct. 1, Ables classified the death of Rhonda Gabriel, 66, as due to the hurricane but didn’t explain why.
On Sept. 30, the Aiken County Coroner’s Office reported a 75-year-old in North Augusta who died of a medical emergency due to the Hurricane, which has knocked out power to most people in the CSRA and water service to many. David Welch, 75, died Friday on Circlewood Drive, according to Ables.
Ables also recorded a previously reported fire death as storm-related. Joyce Barfield, 78, of School Street in Gloverville, died Sunday in a house fire that was started by a candle. Against experts’ advice, some people are using candles instead of flashlights to light their homes during the power outage.
Among the Aiken County deaths were a Beech Island couple, 78-year-old Jerry Savage and his wife, 74-year-old Marcia Savage. They were pronounced dead at 11:40 a.m. after a tree crashed through the roof of their home in the 300 block of Church Road, landing on them.
Also killed was 29-year-old Michael Roukous of Dexter, N.Y., who was pronounced dead at 9:52 a.m. after a tree crashed through the roof of a bed and breakfast home he was renting in the 100 block of Casnettie Road in Beech Island.
Also, 70-year-old Joseph Gullen was pronounced deceased at 8:50 a.m. after a tree crashed through the roof of his home on Metts Park Circle in Aiken.
Burke County
Georgia State Patrol troopers say on Saturday, a traffic light at the intersection of Ga. 121 Bypass and Mike Padgett Highway wasn’t working due to the storm, which resulted in a crash. The crash involved a 2021 Freightliner and a 2014 Honda Accord. The driver of the Honda Accord was pronounced deceased at the crash scene, according to troopers.
Columbia County
In Columbia County, Fortino Dominguez-Gomez, 75, died in Grovetown when a tree fell on a mobile home.
Emanuel County
On Tuesday, a death was reported Emanuel County, according to the Emanuel County Coroner’s Office. Officials say the death involved a tractor and a tree. We are working to learn more.
McDuffie County
McDuffie County Coroner Paul Johnson said four people have been confirmed as victims in that county.
A 27-year-old mother, Kobe Williams, and her two 2-month-old twins Khazmir Williams and Khayzier Williams died in their house in Thomson.
Johnson says 89-year-old Georgia Mae Hampton, of Dearing, also died, but did not release details.

Richmond County
Another death not caused directly by the storm was due to a traffic accident Friday night in Richmond County. Caffee Wright, 52, was pronounced dead on the scene at 10:22 p.m. when a car carrying her struck a fallen tree on Micke Padgett Highway.
Six people died in Richmond County due to trees crashing into homes.
Richmond County Coroner Mark Bowen released the information:
- In the 5000 block of Old Waynesboro Road, Stephen Donehoo, 72, years was pronounced dead on scene after a tree fell on the residence. His great-grandson Izaak Donehoo, 10, was pronounced dead on scene after a tree fell on the residence.
- In the 2100 block of Lake Avenue, Uyen Xuan Le, 36, was pronounced dead on the scene after a tree fell on the residence.
- In the 2200 block of Morningside Drive, Katherine McCall, 62, was pronounced dead on the scene after a tree fell on the residence.
- In the 4500 block of Windsor Spring Road, Andrea Warner, 62, was pronounced dead on the scene after a tree fell on the residence.
- In the 3300 block of Wedgewood Drive, Daverio Carter, 50, was pronounced dead on scene after a tree fell on the residence.
“Our family lost two wonderful souls to the storm,” Michelle Donehoo, Stephen’s daughter and Izaac’s grandmother, posted on Facebook. She posted a link to a GoFundMe to help with funeral expenses.
Sam Carlton said via Facebook that she lost her “little nephew” and “Pops.” She said Izaac would have been 11 in November and he grew up with her son.
“Aaron grew up with his cousin Izaac ... and those of you who knew Steve knew how amazing his soul was,” Carlton said.
Saluda County
The deaths also included two firefighters in Saluda County, 53-year-old Chief Chad Satcher and 18-year-old Probationary Firefighter Landon Bodie, who died when a tree fell on their firetruck while responding to a structure fire. That happened around 6:30 a.m. on Beulah Road about four miles east of Batesburg-Leesville, according to the South Carolina Highway Patrol.
Satcher was the chief of Circle Fire Department and served Saluda County for 35 years.
“We would like to thank our community, state and nation for the outpouring of comfort and support during this difficult time. Please continue to keep our firefighters and families in your thoughts and prayers as they begin to heal from this loss,” said the Saluda County Fire Service in a Facebook post.
There was a third hurricane-related death in Saluda County. The Saluda County Coroner’s Office says 75-year-old Clara Elaine Jackson, of Ridge Spring, was identified as the victim. We don’t have any other details.
MORE FROM NEWS 12:
Washington County
The other two children died early Friday in Washington County, according to Sheriff Joel Cochran.
He said that shortly after 4 a.m., his office got a 911 call reporting that a South Hospital Road home had caught fire. A tree had fallen against the home and trapped two children inside.
The children, Harmony and Derrick Taylor, both died, the sheriff said.
“Words seem inadequate at a time like this, and the Taylor family will need much love and support for years to come. Our WACO family is wrapping out arms around the Taylor family and continuously listing them in prayer,” said the Washington County Public School District
